observations.summary: A repository test passed while asserting the opposite of the contract named in its own comment. Mutating the --fail-on-drift exit expression so the gate fails every clean sweep left all 16 tests green, so a broken opt-in gate would have shipped behind a green Gate A.

success_criteria: Mutating a contract predicate that a test names causes at least one test in the repository suite to fail, demonstrated by running the mutation.
The check derives its subjects rather than reading a hand-kept list, so a newly added contract enrolls without editing the checker.
Every existing suite and Gate A step stays green under the unmutated tree, with no test weakened to accommodate the check.
The change playbook rule that currently scopes mutation proof to validator rules is restated to cover any newly asserted contract, or the narrower scope is defended in writing.

monitoring_plan.criterion: After promotion, a deliberate mutation of a covered contract predicate continues to fail at least one test, and Gate A remains green on the unmutated tree.

lesson.reason: A control is prepared and under human review, not accepted. scripts/mutation_guard.py derives each test file's subject module from the test's own source, applies single-point AST mutations, and reports mutants the suite fails to notice. The rule was broadened from validator rules to any newly asserted contract in all three places that state it — AGENTS.md, .github/pull_request_template.md, and docs/rules.md — after review found the first attempt had changed only AGENTS.md, leaving the narrow wording standing at the template where the rule is actually applied. Demonstrated against the incident itself: at the default unbounded budget the guard generates the exact operand-drop mutation at packet_drift.py:405 that survived all sixteen tests before the fix, and the current suite kills it in 17 seconds. It is a deliberate command rather than a Gate A step because a full sweep runs the suite once per mutant, following the routing-eval precedent. lesson.status stays pending until a human merges it.

disposition_reason: Recorded at observed. A recurring normalized fleet failure with one precisely evidenced instance and one documented prior occurrence qualifies for a typed record under the improvement lifecycle. A control has since been prepared and is described in lesson.reason, but no formal attempt is appended, no independent evaluation has occurred, and no promotion is claimed or authorized by this record.
limitations: The earlier occurrence is known only from AGENTS.md prose and has no incident record, so the recurrence claim rests on one precisely evidenced instance plus that documented prior.
The observation source is added in the same commit as this record, so source.revision is null; no prior revision binds it.

Severity high reflects consequence if unfixed rather than realised impact: the defect was caught by adversarial review before merge, but a false-green test undermines every other claim the fleet's gates make.
The semantic improvement validators are parked at tag pre-trim-2026-08-02, so only the schema layer of this record is enforced today; its lifecycle legality is a written contract, not a checked one.
Gate A was green throughout the incident and is not implicated: it is structural by design and never asserted this contract.

No formal attempt is appended and status stays observed. The attempt contract requires calibration and regression case sets and an evaluation record, and this fleet's rule is that a fresh context or deterministic oracle evaluates what the author prepared. Self-asserting those fields would be the same bulk self-approval this fleet rejects, so the prepared control is described in lesson.reason and left for an authorized owner to evaluate and promote. An independent verification-engineer run has now executed the control at 8f0c81ae992f742c1edfe272dc6b4d63746c74a9 and returned pass on all seven checks, but recording that evidence is not the same as promoting the record; the status transition remains an owner decision.

The control's first version carried the defect it exists to prevent, found by adversarial review before merge: it never ran the test against unmutated code, so a suite failing for any unrelated reason — a missing dependency, the wrong working directory — scored every mutant as killed and printed PASS. A baseline run now raises UnverifiablePair instead. The same review found its documented default budget could not reach the mutation cited above (index 35 of 48 under a prefix of 12); the default is now unbounded and a bounded --limit samples evenly across the walk.

The guard is a sampling tool, not a proof. --limit bounds mutants per module, its operator set is small (boolean-operand drop, comparison swap, not-removal, boolean-constant flip), and a survivor may be semantically equivalent rather than a defect. A clean report means no survivor among the mutants tried, never that a suite is complete.

Correction: an earlier version of this record stated that scripts/test_readonly_guard.py was uncovered because readonly-guard.py is hyphenated and no convention derives it. Review surfaced that the same file was simultaneously enrolled as a false subject of an unrelated eval test, so the guard would have mutated the fleet's fail-closed security control against a test that never invokes it. The sibling convention now tries the hyphenated spelling, so the pairing is correct and that limitation no longer holds.

A second review round found the control's reporting layer repeated the original incident in miniature: every decision lived in an untested main(), including three newly asserted exit codes, added by the very commit that broadened the rule to require tests for exit codes. main() now has exit-code tests, and each was confirmed by inverting its branch and watching the naming test fail. The collapse of all-mutants-survived pairs was also narrowed to inferred subjects only: collapsing sibling pairs too would have hidden the most severe finding the tool can produce behind known-benign path-string artifacts, trading one false clean for another.

Independent execution evidence, 2026-08-07, revision 8f0c81ae992f742c1edfe272dc6b4d63746c74a9: run in a network-isolated, read-only, digest-pinned container by sde-agents:verification-engineer. Gate A 25/25, 18 guard tests, validate_improvements PASS. The central claim reproduced exactly - the operand-drop mutant is index 35 of 48 at packet_drift.py:405, the suite kills it via the test that owns that contract, and the module is restored byte-identical. All five exit-code contracts confirmed against fresh fixtures, including that a vacuous sibling pair stays a finding at exit 1 rather than collapsing. Before this, every green claim about this control traced only to the author's terminal.

Three defects remain open in the control, found by that verification and NOT fixed. (1) The unexercised claim is still gated on a sampled count: the rule is len(survivors) == tried where tried is the sample size, so under --limit a subject that IS exercised can still be labelled 'probably never exercises it'. Narrowing collapse to inferred subjects reduced the blast radius without closing the mechanism; the claim should additionally require an unbounded run. At the prior revision this suppressed 58+ real survivors, 26 of them in validate_fleet.py. (2) A negative --limit exits 2, colliding with EXIT_REFUSED, in a tool whose stated design is that a collapsed exit status cannot distinguish refused-to-run from ran-and-proved-nothing. (3) A --limit of 12 also misses the motivating mutant, because even spacing lands on indices 34 and 38; the docstring says only a prefix budget would exclude it, which invites the wrong inference.

The bounded sweep surfaced real coverage gaps elsewhere in the fleet, discovered but not fixed and not owned by this record: entry validation in migrate_v1_to_v2.py:59 and migrate_v2_to_v3.py:59 is never executed by the test that enrols them; the auth-marker detector at clean_room.py:236 is unpinned (security-adjacent); and branches in evidence_envelope.py and graders.py go unexercised. Equivalent mutants, such as swapping the comparison in a module's __main__ guard, are unfiltered noise that will recur.
